title: refactor: remove custom MCP servers from agents
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Removes per-agent custom MCP URLs, headers, credential encryption, and third-party runtime loading until reusable account-level MCPs are designed.
- Stores enabled MCP server IDs in `mcpServers`; `pollinations` is the only supported ID and keeps caller-token forwarding plus the generation/discovery tool allowlist.
- Simplifies the agent dashboard, API, catalog integration, CLI output, and tests around the built-in server.
- Migrates legacy `pollinationsTools` configs to the ID array, removes embedded custom definitions, and drops `agent.mcp_headers_ciphertext`.

Deployment note: the D1 migration and new Enter Worker must remain paired; the existing production workflow applies migrations immediately before deployment.

Checks: Enter 25/25 focused tests, Gen managed-agent integration, Enter/Gen typechecks, Biome, Drizzle check, seeded legacy migration test, and all 51 migrations on fresh local D1.

gist.headline: One tool shed, tidied
gist.blurb: Managed agents now keep their tools in one small, well-labeled shed. Pollinations MCP remains wired in, with token forwarding and its generation and discovery tools ready to go.
gist.summary: Managed agents now store enabled MCP server IDs in `mcpServers`, supporting the built-in `pollinations` server with caller-token forwarding and generation/discovery tool allowlists while legacy `pollinationsTools`, custom URLs, headers, encrypted credentials, and runtime loading are migrated away.
gist.impact: Agent creators get a simpler dashboard, API, catalog, and CLI centered on the built-in Pollinations MCP, while the platform prepares reusable account-level MCP connections.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful gardener-organizer clearing a cluttered tool shed of mismatched cables and unlabeled toolboxes, leaving one friendly Pollinations-branded MCP terminal connected to healthy code-plants. The monitor robot can eagerly hold a neat ID label reading `mcpServers`, showing that agent tools are now a simpler built-in setup.
